Try the prototype

From One‑Off Consult to the Vet Who Checks Back

PetDoc wins the first visit (4.8 stars, NPS 65), then disappears from the owner's life: only 21.2% of new owners come back within 180 days. The visit ends when the call ends. This strategy makes PetDoc check back after an acute visit and remember the pet when the owner returns.

I built this as the case study for the Senior Product Manager, Patient Experience role. Every section is a judgment call: which problem to solve and for whom, what to test first, what not to build, and where the leverage sits.

What are we solving?

What happens after the call. Acute owners, 61% of new owners, hear nothing once it ends, and only 0.7% come back within 14 days. Owners who do return are often asked to re-tell the story.

01The goal 02Problem framing 03Target audience

01The goal

What is Care Loop?

After an acute visit, the vet sets a check-in day. On that day PetDoc asks “How is Bella today?” “Better” closes the case. “Same” or “worse” becomes a one-tap re-check with the same vet, with the notes and photo attached. A red flag always goes to in-person care.

It is the lead bet, about half of the +4.7pp programme; the memory fix and the care plan add the rest. See how it works step by step or try it in the prototype.

Terms used from here
Acute, unclear
The two visit types Care Loop serves, 66% of owners
Episode
One acute problem, from the consultation to closure, re-booking, escalation or expiry
Re-check
A follow-up consultation for the same episode; a normal paid visit
RC, IP, EXP, KR
Root cause (section 2), initiative (5), experiment (8), key result (below)

One bet carries the goal, one foundation makes it work. Key results show it is working, and guardrails show what must not break.

02Where second visits leak

The gap is not consult quality; it is everything around the consult. A family vet keeps owners by knowing the pet and checking back. PetDoc's journey does neither, and the 4.8-star rating hides it.

Each step of the owner journey, what goes wrong, and what the data says it costs. Severity combines how many owners it hits and how much it cuts return.

Root causes

RC1
The consult is a transaction, not an episode

No follow-up moment exists after the call

Evidence: acute 14-day return 0.7%
RC2
Context does not travel

Intake and history do not reach the vet, even within one visit

Evidence: re-telling on 19% of first and 23% of second visits
RC3
Ratings measure the call, not the relationship

The team optimises what it sees: a 4.8-star call

Evidence: ratings track return (5-star 32% vs 21%), but 68% of 5-star raters still never return, and re-telling barely dents the rating
RC4
No plan for predictable needs

Young animals have a known schedule; PetDoc ignores it

Evidence: young animal 25.7% return on a 45-day cadence
RC5
Reliability friction

Video, uploads and delivery fail often enough to matter

Evidence: up to +3.0pp if fully removed (model ceiling); owned by other missions
RC6
Nobody measures context loss

Re-telling is invisible on today's dashboards

Evidence: no “vet knew my pet” metric exists

Data caveats (the first visit in the sample may not be the first ever; no vet ID or diagnosis; small chronic group) are in Appendix B.

Judgment call

Why lead with RC1 and not RC2?

RC2 has the strongest evidence, but even removing re-telling entirely, and assuming the whole association is causal, adds only +1.6pp. RC1 is the only cause large enough to move the goal, so I bet on it and de-risk it with a three-week concierge test. RC2 is fixed alongside, because a re-check that makes the owner re-tell recreates the problem.

Judgment call

Why not lead with the new pet parent?

They already return at almost twice the acute rate, and a care plan needs an engine plus a clinic-leakage test. The care manager returns at 51%; the job there is not to break it with re-telling.

What do we build?

Care Loop. The vet sets a check-in day, PetDoc asks “How is Bella today?”, and “same” or “worse” becomes a one-tap re-check with the same vet and the notes attached. The prototype is that moment, clickable.

The three are one cycle, not three features. Care Loop is the Follow up lever. Every closed episode feeds the pet record (Remember). The record personalises the care plan (Plan ahead). The plan and the check-in create the next visit (Follow up), which adds to the record again.

Positioning

Competitors sell the same thing PetDoc does: a good one-off video consult, often free through insurers. None visibly owns what happens after the call. PetDoc can't win on price or 24/7 availability; it can win on

“the vet who remembers your pet and checks back.”

Competitive detail is in Appendix A.

Judgment call

Why sequence Follow up and Remember first, when Plan ahead is more than a quarter of the lift?

The care plan needs a plan engine and species and age data we don't capture yet. It also faces a real risk: vaccinations need an in-person visit, so bookings may leak to local clinics. Follow up and Remember ship on data we have, and they build the record the plan needs.

What we chose not to do

Free or discounted re-checks. Pricing is fixed in the brief; a free visit is a pricing change, not a product change.

Subscription or membership. Out of scope for the same reason, even though it works for Airvet in the US.

Broadcast nudges, content and win-back pushes. Acute owners most likely return around day 70 with a new problem, which a message cannot create. More pushes would also dull the Care Loop check-in.

LLM-written clinical summaries in v1. A wrong summary in a clinical context costs trust we can't buy back. v1 shows structured data; an AI summary with sources and vet confirmation is a Year 2 option.

Our own pharmacy logistics. Delivery speed matters (return drops from 25.7% to 11.6% once delivery takes 6+ days), but it belongs to Ops and the partner pharmacy. We track it and push.

Judgment call

Why IP-1B before the full record (IP-2A)?

Re-telling happens on 19% of first visits, where no history exists yet. Showing the vet what the owner already typed is cheaper than building a record, and it removes the cause on visit one. The record follows once episodes exist to fill it.

Why is IP-3B conditional?

A free follow-up costs unpaid vet time against a €10 margin, cannibalises the paid re-check, and touches fixed pricing. It ships only if the experiments show owners want reassurance, not a visit.

06Care Loop deep dive

The vet sets a check-in day; on that day PetDoc asks “How is Bella today?” and turns “same” or “worse” into a one-tap re-check with the same vet and the full story attached.

Scope. Care Loop is the check-in, the three answers and the one-tap re-check (IP-1A). The care summary (IP-1C) sets it up, and the vet pre-call view carries the story into the re-check. Both ship with it in Q1.

Hypothesis

If the vet sets a check-in day during an acute visit, and PetDoc asks the owner on that day with a one-tap re-check, then owners whose pet is not improving will come back to PetDoc instead of waiting or going to a clinic. Acute 14-day re-checks rise from 0.7% to at least 4%, without hurting ratings, creating unneeded visits, or lowering new-episode return. The data can't tell whether today's non-returners recovered or went elsewhere; the concierge test asks them.

The decision point is the check-in screen: do owners answer, how many say “same” or “worse”, and do they book? That is what the prototype covers.

The flow

What design and engineering need

Rules set with the medical lead; no model in v1.

InputRule
Condition groupDefault check-in day, for example 2 days for stomach upsets and unclear cases, 3 for wounds, eyes and ears, 5 for skin. Final defaults come from the medical lead.
Rx not delivered by the check-in dayMove the check-in to delivery plus 2 days
No answerOne reminder after 24 hours; expire after 72 hours and show a “book a consultation” card instead
“Same”, inside the vet's expected windowReassure (“this is normal until Friday”), offer “ask me again in 2 days” or a re-check
“Same”, outside the windowLead with the re-check
“Worse”Three red-flag questions. Any red flag: in-person guidance and the nearest clinic. None: priority re-check with the same vet, else the next vet within 2 hours
Vet switched it offNo check-in; the reason is logged
Rules
A re-check is a normal paid consultation; no discounts, because pricing is fixed.
At most two prompts per episode: the check-in and one reminder after 24 hours. Transactional updates (care summary, Rx status) and an owner-requested “ask me again” don't count; nothing promotional is sent.
The check-in is a service message tied to the consultation, not marketing; legal confirms the consent basis.
Red-flag routing to in-person care is a safety requirement, not an option.
One active Care Loop per pet per episode; multi-pet owners get one per pet.

User stories and acceptance criteria

All in the MVP. The criteria are the definition of done for each story.

StoryAcceptance criteria
CL-1As a vet, I want to pick a condition group and have the check-in day pre-filledso that it takes about 15 secondsVet Experience
  • Given I close an acute consultation, when I pick a condition group, then the day fills from the default and I can edit it.
  • Given I switch it off, then I give a reason and nothing is sent.
CL-2As an owner, I want a plain summary right after the callso that I know the home care, red flags, check-in date and Rx statusCare Loop team
  • Given the vet saves the note, then I get the summary in the app and by email, templated with no extra vet writing.
  • Given notifications are off, then permission is asked once, in context, and email is the fallback.
CL-3As an owner, I want to be asked on the day the vet chose, with one reminder at mostso that I do not have to remember and am not naggedCare Loop team
  • Given a check-in day is set, then one check-in goes out, by push with email as fallback, and an in-app card always shows.
  • Given the Rx is late, then it moves to delivery plus 2 days.
  • Given I have not answered, then one reminder follows after 24 hours, and after 72 hours it expires with a “book a consultation” card.
CL-4As an owner whose pet is better, I want to say so in one tapso that the case closesCare Loop team
  • Given I tap “Better”, then the episode closes, is saved to the pet record, and I see one skippable question: “Did the vet already know Bella?”
CL-5As an owner whose pet is the same, I want to be told what is normalso that I only book a vet when it is neededCare Loop team
  • Given I tap “Same” inside the vet's window, then I see reassurance, and can ask again in 2 days or book. The reminder does not count toward the two prompts.
  • Given I am outside the window, then the re-check leads.
CL-6As an owner whose pet is worse, I want three red-flag questionsso that a serious case goes to in-person care and the rest to a vet fastCare Loop team
  • Given any answer is a red flag, then I see urgent in-person guidance and the nearest clinic, and the episode is logged as escalated.
  • Given there is none, then a priority re-check is offered with the same vet, else the next within 2 hours.
  • The red-flag questions and routing cannot be switched off by a flag or config change.
CL-7As an owner, I want to book the re-check in one tapso that I do not retell the storyCare Loop team
  • Given I choose a re-check, then the price shows before I confirm, and the reason, last note, meds, answer and photo are attached.
CL-8As a vet, I want one pre-call screen for a re-checkso that I know the case before I say helloVet Experience
  • Given a re-check is booked, then I see the last note, meds, answer and photo on one screen; if the photo is still uploading, the rest loads first.
CL-9As the data analyst, I want each owner assigned once to Care Loop or a holdoutso that the test is readableData
  • Given an owner is eligible, then they are assigned by owner and keep it across episodes.
  • Given they are in the holdout, then no check-in is sent, but their events are still recorded with the arm.

Edge cases

Proposed behaviour; engineering confirms what is feasible.

SituationExpected behaviour
Owner answers after it expiredShow the “book a consultation” card. Nothing more is sent.
Owner answers on a second deviceState is server-side, so iOS, Android and web show the same card, and a second answer is ignored.
Owner has more than one petOne Care Loop per pet, each named on its own card.
No vet free within 2 hoursOffer the next slot with the time shown. Red-flag guidance is never held back.
Push fails or is offSend email, and always show the in-app card.
Scheduler retriesOne check-in per episode and attempt, so a retry never double-sends.

Every event carries episode_id, pet_id, arm and timestamp. They create the labels the case data lacks: condition, vet judgment and owner-reported outcome.

EventFires whenFeeds

Risks designed in before build

Full price for a re-check

A re-check is a normal paid visit, with the price shown before booking and reassurance first on “same”. If owners balk, move it to the low end of the €35 to €45 band. Legal confirms the fee rules; EXP-007 tests whether it feels like an upsell.

When the pet is worse

The vet sees the new photo and the original notes, then adjusts treatment or refers the owner in person with a written hand-over. Red flags go to a clinic and are logged as “escalated”.

Clinical liability

The app never diagnoses. “Normal until Friday” is the vet's recovery window, the medical lead signs off the red-flag questions, and every “worse” answer reaches a vet or a clinic. Legal confirms the remote-treatment and device rules before launch.

Will vets set the check-in?

The field sits in the closing note vets already write, so there is no extra writing; “15 seconds” is a target, timed in co-design. To confirm: re-checks are paid vet work, and same-vet routing needs the production vet ID.

If Vet Experience can't ship this quarter

Care Loop v0 runs on segment defaults the medical lead signs off, and re-checks go to the next available vet. IP-1B and KR3 move to Q2, with a lower answer rate assumed.

Owners who simply recovered

Most acute cases resolve, so many owners will answer “better”: the episode closes and is saved to the record. The bet is on the 25 to 30% who answer “same” or “worse”; the concierge test measures that share before build.

Two things are under test: the concierge email that proves the moment before anything is built, and the in-app check-in with what follows it. That is where owners either come back or don't. The other flows show the rest of the portfolio for context.

How do we prove it?

A three-week concierge test with a holdout before anything is built, then an A/B test from week 7. One north star, split by episode, and guardrails that can stop a rollout on their own.

08Experiments 09Metrics

08Ten tests, three phases, pre-registered

Every assumption is a bet with a number on it. Each test has one primary metric, a minimum detectable effect, a sample size and a decision rule written before launch. Each test links to the prototype screen where it runs. Samples assume 80% power and 5% significance; principles are in Appendix C.

Decision rule for every testWritten down before launch, applied at full sample.
Shipif the primary metric clears the effect size and guardrails hold
Iterateif it is positive but below
Killif it is flat or negative at full sample

Weeks 1 to 6, little or no build. Proves the moment is real before engineering commits.

IDTestHypothesis with effect sizePrimary metricPrototype
EXP-001Concierge check-in
Test
Manual push or email to acute and unclear owners, on a day set by the medical lead's default table from the vet's note.
Base case
40% answer, 30% say “same” or “worse”, 45% of those book, so 14-day re-checks reach about 4% vs about 0.7% in the holdout.
Go
Re-checks are at least 4% and significantly above the holdout.
Kill
Answers fall below 25%, or “same or worse” below 20% (the low case).
Iterate
Anything in between.
Also ask
Non-bookers: did the pet recover, or did they go to a clinic?
14-day re-check, contacted vs holdout

EXP-004“Vet knew my pet” baselineNot an A/B: one tap after each visit sets the baseline for KR3 and RC6Response rate at least 30%

Weeks 7 to 16, the Care Loop MVP. Tests whether the built product beats no check-in. Traffic: about 425 eligible new owners a week (1,840 a month), split 50/50. The 14-day read (about 330 per arm) is enrolled by week 9 and read in week 12. The 30-day read (about 530 per arm) comes in week 15. The 180-day sample (2,050 per arm) is enrolled by week 16 and read in month 10. Only EXP-008 runs alongside, as a declared second factor inside the Care Loop arm. All other design tests wait for the rollout in Phase 3, so no owner sees two tests at the same moment.

EXP-008Care summary with a named check-in dateNaming the day lifts answer rate from 40% to 48%Answer rate

Q2 to Q3, after rollout. Care Loop goes to 90% of eligible owners, with a 10% holdout kept to confirm the 180-day result. The three design tests each sit at a different moment of the episode (check-in day, “same” screen, booking routing), and their factors are declared upfront.

Judgment call

Why a concierge test before any build?

The riskiest assumption is that enough acute pets are still unwell on day 3. That costs a form and an email list to test, not six weeks of engineering. Until the week-6 read, engineering builds only no-regret pieces (episode model, events, care summary). The check-in flow is built behind a flag and only switched on if the concierge test passes.

Why split it?

Care Loop adds same-episode re-checks by design. If only that part rises, we moved the number, not the relationship. The long-run proof that Care Loop works is new-episode return: owners who were checked on come back to PetDoc for the next problem too.

How does it ship?

Vet Experience and the medical lead come in during discovery, not at hand-off. Q1 proves Care Loop, and each quarter builds on the last until PetDoc is the app owners open between problems.

Why a shared metric with Vet Experience?

Their goal is a better vet workflow, not my return rate. A shared metric they already care about (re-telling rate with stable call length) turns my ask into their win, and gives both teams the same dashboard.

The pet record becomes the platform

Owner-controlled sharing with local clinics, insurer partnerships that bring free-consult users onto a paid relationship, and AI-assisted summaries that a vet confirms. That is how PetDoc becomes the app owners open between problems, which is the company's stated ambition.

Care Loop funnel

Every input is my assumption, not data, and each one has a test. Delivery assumes typical push-plus-email reach. Answer, “same or worse” and booking rates are measured by the concierge test (EXP-001) and EXP-005. The incremental share has a ceiling: only 14.3% of acute owners return within 180 days anyway, so at most about 14% of re-checks are pull-forward. The rest of the 25% haircut covers re-checks that cannibalise the next new-episode visit. EXP-005 measures both directly through new-episode return in each arm.

How the Care Loop lift is calculated

The base case, step by step. Low and high use the same formula with their own column of the funnel above. The result is a modelled estimate: the segment mix is data, every funnel rate is an assumption that EXP-001 and EXP-005 test.

StepCalculationResult
Eligible ownersAcute 736 + unclear 54 = 790 of 1,200 owners66%, about 1,840 of 2,800 new owners a month
Eligible owners who book a re-check85% delivered × 40% answer × 30% “same” or “worse” × 45% book4.6%, about 85 bookings a month
Keep only the incremental ones4.6% × 75% would not have returned anyway3.4% of eligible owners
Scale to all new owners3.4% × 66% eligible+2.3pp
New 180-day rate21.2% today + 2.3pp23.5%

Business value

Each +1pp is about 28 extra second visits and 8 third visits per monthly cohort: about €4.3k contribution, or €17k revenue, per year from new owners.

Per new owner, first 180 daysTodayCare Loop onlyProgramme (base)
Consultations per owner (includes 28% going on to a third)1.271.301.33
Contribution at €10 per consultation€12.71€13.01€13.32
Added contribution per year, new cohortsabout €10kabout €20k

Why fund it anyway. The direct number is small, and I don't hide it. The MVP costs roughly €50k (about 3 engineers for 6 weeks at an assumed €140k loaded annual cost). On new owners alone, that pays back in about five years. The case rests on four things:

  • The base is bigger than new owners. Care Loop runs on every acute consultation, including returning owners. The case data only covers new owners, so I size total acute volume from the warehouse in week 1. If returning owners bring as many acute consultations as new owners, the direct value doubles to about €20k a year for Care Loop and €40k for the programme.
  • Retention instead of acquisition. The programme adds €0.61 contribution per new owner within 180 days, which is +4.8% for the same acquisition spend. To match that through acquisition, Growth would need to cut CAC by €0.61 on every one of 2,800 owners a month.
  • Value compounds after 180 days. Owners with a second visit go on to a third at 28%, so the 180-day window understates lifetime value.
  • The record is the moat. Every closed episode builds a pet record that free insurer hotlines don't have. It is also the data the care plan (Q2) needs.

BData, method and caveatsDataset, model, sample sizes and what a reviewer should know

Every number in the case is re-computed from the CSV.

ItemDetail
Dataset1,413 consultations, 1,200 owners, 1 Aug 2025 to 31 Jan 2026; extracted 1 Aug 2026, so every consultation has a full 180 days
Unit for retentionEach owner's first consultation in the sample (1,200)
ModelLogistic regression of 180-day return on segment, re-telling, video issue, upload failure, Rx delivery of 5+ days, wait time, consultation length and platform. Reported odds ratios are associations, not causal effects.
Friction sizingSet each friction to zero, keep the segment mix, compare predicted return: re-telling +1.6pp, video +1.5, upload +0.8, Rx +0.7; +4.8pp for all four. These are upper bounds, not forecasts. They assume each friction is removed completely and that the whole association is causal. The frictions also overlap (restarts sit inside video issues), so the parts are not strictly additive.
Rx delivery effectAmong the 459 owners with a prescription, the effect is a step, not a slope: 25.7% return when delivery takes up to 5 days (373 owners), 11.6% at 6+ days (86). The case uses the step.
Sample sizesTwo-proportion test, 80% power, 5% significance, two-sided
Caveats a reviewer should know
The first visit in the sample may not be the owner's first visit on PetDoc. Week 1: replicate with full history.
54% of first visits are unrated, and unrated owners return less (18.8% vs 24.0%), so ratings are biased upward.
No vet ID and no diagnosis column. Same-vet routing and condition-specific timing cannot be sized from this data.
consultation_restarted is a subset of video_audio_issue (all 54 restarts also had video issues).
Chronic (149 owners), unclear (54) and the tech-plus-re-telling group (31) are small: read them as direction.
The friction findings are observational from 1,200 owners. The model adjusts for segment and the other frictions, but frictions co-occur and the source of the re-telling flag is unknown. Only an experiment (EXP-003) proves cause.
CExperimentation principlesEight rules that govern every test

Eight rules govern every test, so a result we ship is a result we can trust.

01

One primary metric per test

Picking the winning metric afterwards is how teams fool themselves

02

Pre-register the effect size and sample

No power calculations after the fact; no peeking to stop early

03

Guardrails on every test

A return win that raises “not needed” re-checks or opt-outs is a loss

04

Read by persona and condition group

A win for stomach upsets may be noise for skin; ship per group

05

Randomise by owner, one test per moment

An owner in the timing test is not also in the named-date test; nested tests are declared upfront

06

Keep a holdout for the 180-day read

180-day return and new-episode return only show up months later

07

Clinical review before launch

Any test that changes what owners are told about their pet's health is signed off by the medical lead

08

Ship or learn

A failed test is logged with what it taught; we never rerun the same test, we build on it

DHow to measure the hard metricsRe-telling, incremental re-checks, same vs new episode

None of these metrics exists at PetDoc today, so each definition is agreed before launch.

MetricDefinitionLogged from
Re-telling ratePrimary: consultations where the owner answers “no” to “did the vet already know your pet?”, divided by consultations answered. Secondary: the vet flag “asked for information already provided”. A vet flagging their own lapse is biased low, so it is only a cross-check.Owner survey; vet tool flag
Incremental re-check rateRe-checks within 14 days in the treated arm minus the control arm, per eligible ownerEpisode table; bookings
Same vs new episodeA return within 14 days of a Care Loop episode, or within 30 days with the same condition group, is the same episode. Any other return is a new episodeEpisode table; condition group
Answer rateCheck-ins answered divided by check-ins delivered (not sent)Notification and in-app events
“Not needed” shareRe-checks the vet marks “not needed” divided by re-checks completedVet tool flag
Pull-forward checkCompare 180-day return excluding same-episode re-checks between arms. If treated is not higher, the lift was borrowed, not createdHoldout and episode table

Scoping decisions to agree before launch

DecisionRecommended default
Which consultations are eligibleAcute and unclear, first and returning owners; chronic excluded
Attribution window for a re-check14 days from the check-in; extend to 30 days as a secondary read. Why 14: the shortest window in the data, long enough to cover a day 2 to 5 check-in, and well before the day-70 median return
Owners with several petsOne episode per pet; randomise by owner so siblings share an arm
Delivered vs sentA check-in counts as delivered only when push or email is confirmed, or the in-app card is shown
EGlossaryTerms and abbreviations used in the case
North star
The 180-day second-consultation rate for new owners
Care Loop
The lead bet: vet-set check-in after an acute visit, with a one-tap re-check that carries context
Episode
One acute problem, from the consultation to closure, re-booking, escalation or expiry
Re-check
A follow-up consultation for the same episode; a normal paid visit
New-episode return
A return for a different problem, after day 14
Re-telling
The vet asks for information the owner already provided
Condition group
A short list of acute problem types the vet picks at the end of the call; sets the check-in day
Red flag
A symptom that means in-person care now; routes the owner out of the app
Concierge test
A manual version of the feature, run before building it
Arm
One group in a test. The treated arm gets the feature; the control arm, or holdout, does not
MDE
Minimum detectable effect: the smallest lift a test is powered to see
Holdout
Owners kept out of a feature long-term to measure long-term effects
Pull-forward
A return that would have happened anyway, just earlier
pp
Percentage points
Odds ratio
How much a factor multiplies the odds of returning; below 1 means it lowers return
MAU
Monthly active users
CAC
Customer acquisition cost
Vet Experience, Growth
The neighbouring missions: everything vets do on the platform; acquisition and new user groups
